subject: SLA discussion: uptime target, P95 latency carveouts, and monthly credit floor
messages:
From: Kelly Turner <kelly@altitudeanalytics.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@altitudeanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA ask and a couple carveouts

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the inference throughput looked promising. Procurement asked me to start formalizing the SLA so we can move the PoC forward. A couple of questions up front: 

- Can Redwood commit to a 99.95% monthly uptime for our hosted model endpoints? Altitude is processing near-real-time analytics and that threshold is our target for public SLAs.
- We run a daily bulk scoring job (03:00–04:30 PT) that spikes CPU/GPU for batched inference. Would you consider an explicit maintenance/exception window for that workload so it doesn’t count against uptime?

We attached a short checklist (we can share DocuSign/contract later). Happy to jump on a short call to walk through specifics.

Best,
Kelly
Procurement Lead | Altitude Analytics

Attachment: ALT_requirement_summary.csv (stub)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Kelly Turner <kelly@altitudeanalytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask and a couple carveouts

Hi Kelly — thanks, and glad the demo was useful. Quick answers and next steps below.

- Uptime: Our standard hosted SLA template defaults to 99.9% monthly availability for general-purpose endpoints. We can discuss moving to 99.95% for a committed revenue band; the tradeoffs are higher reserved capacity and different credit mechanics.
- Batched job carveout: We can add a scheduled-maintenance carveout for a defined daily window. We usually require the window to be explicitly declared in the mutual action plan and limited to recurring maintenance or pre-declared bulk-processing windows.

I’m looping in Ben (account lead) and Laura (legal) to coordinate commercial/contract points. I’ll draft a proposal that shows: 1) what 99.95% looks like month-to-month, 2) the monthly credit formula, and 3) how scheduled batch windows are excluded.

Proposed next step: Ben to send a short commercial counter-proposal today; Laura will review redlines and share any legal constraints. If that works, can you share the expected monthly token volume for the PoC?

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Kelly Turner <kelly@altitudeanalytics.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood commercial offer (baseline + optional uplift)

Kelly — following up with a commercial baseline and an optional upgrade for 99.95%: 

Baseline (standard hosted):
- Availability commitment: 99.9% monthly
- Remedy: service credit equal to 5% of monthly invoice for each distinct outage band (per template), capped at 50% of that month’s fee

Optional uplift (99.95% target):
- Higher availability commitment: 99.95% monthly
- Remedy: pro-rata credit computed as (Missed uptime percent / 100) * monthly fee, with a minimum monthly credit floor of $5,000 and a cap at 100% of the month’s invoice for the first 3 months of a committed annual contract
- Commercial uplift: incremental per-token rate for reserved capacity (outlined in attachment).

Batched-inference carveout proposal: explicitly exclude a single recurring maintenance window (default suggestion: 03:00–04:30 PT daily) from uptime calculations, provided it’s declared in the MOU and automated page alerts are sent 24h in advance for any deviations.

Next steps: If Altitude agrees conceptually, Laura will send a redline of the SLA_Draft (I’ve attached the pricing appendix). Marcus, can you confirm whether the carveout will affect caching/KV lifetimes for large-batch runs?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Draft_Altitude_v2.pdf; Pricing_Appendix_ALT_v1.xlsx

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial offer (baseline + optional uplift)

Ben / team — technical note on the batched carveout:

- KV cache and prefix-caching: If the daily bulk job runs within the carveout window and we intentionally allow longer batch durations, KV cache eviction may cause cold-start token overhead outside of the window. We can mitigate with:
  - pinned warm nodes for the job (adds reserved-cost)
  - short TTL bump during the declared run window

- Latency SLOs: For batched jobs we usually treat P95 differently. If Altitude wants the same interactive P95 (e.g., <250ms) for both interactive and bulk workloads, cost/architecture changes are required. My recommendation:
  - Keep interactive endpoints under the 99.95% P95 target.
  - Define bulk-scoring endpoints with a looser P95 (e.g., <1500ms) and explicitly exclude them from the interactive latency SLA.

Happy to get on a short call with Altitude’s infra team to review the expected traffic profile.

—Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kelly Turner <kelly@altitudeanalytics.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@altitudeanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial offer (baseline + optional uplift)

Thanks Ben / team — we reviewed the optional uplift and have internal constraints: 

- Procurement prefers a single SLA that covers both interactive and batch endpoints; splitting latency buckets complicates our external customer-facing promises. Is it possible to support a single documented SLA but include a limited monthly exception for bulk scoring that does not trigger credits if the job runs within the declared window?
- The $5,000 minimum credit floor for uplift is acceptable as a transition, but we need a cap of no greater than 100% of the monthly invoice.

Action items from our side: I’ve attached a short redline (SLA_redline_Altitude_v1.docx) showing suggested language. Can Laura review legal redlines and confirm if Redwood is comfortable with the single-SLA-with-declaration exception approach?

Kelly
Procurement Lead | Altitude Analytics

Attachment: SLA_redline_Altitude_v1.docx

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Kelly Turner <kelly@altitudeanalytics.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial offer (baseline + optional uplift)

Kelly — thanks for the redline. Quick legal and commercial position: 

- Single SLA with declared-exception: Acceptable with conditions. We will publish a single SLA document covering uptime and latency, and we will add a paragraph that specifies: (a) explicitly-declared recurring batch windows are excluded from uptime calculations for the purpose of service credits, and (b) any deviation from declared windows that causes unplanned downtime will be measured against the SLA.
- Latency: because Altitude needs a single SLA, we propose defining two service classes in the contract (interactive and batch) but keep a single headline SLA table for public-facing language; the credit triggers will reference the declared class per endpoint. This preserves Altitude’s single-SLA promise while giving us operational clarity.
- Credit floor/cap: We can accept a $5,000 minimum monthly floor for the optional uplift and confirm the cap at 100% of the invoice.

Olga / Ben — I’ll incorporate these points into a redline and return by Monday. Kelly — once we land language, we’ll update HubSpot and circulate an MOU with the declared batch windows.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_redline_olga_20270506.docx
